concept_summary: A restaurant at 401 Columbus Ave, North Beach, upgrading from its current Type 41 (beer/wine) authorization to a Type 47 (full liquor) ABC license, with no tenant improvements or physical expansion in the existing ~2,570 sq ft space.

overall.line: Of the 4 approvals this concept needs: 2 further review (zoning and use, alcohol licence), 1 insufficient information (building permit and change of use), 1 allowed (health permit).
overall.next_step: Confirm in writing with SF Planning Department whether the concept is formula retail and whether the proposal changes any condition of the five Conditional Use Authorizations on file at this address (1988–2010), then file the Conditional Use Authorization application with a pre-application meeting…

approvals.summary: Upgrading the existing restaurant to serve full liquor requires a Conditional Use Authorization from the Planning Commission because the North Beach Special Use District treats a restaurant serving on-sale liquor as a conditional use and intensifying an existing conditional use requires a new CUA.

findings.text: The address sits in the North Beach NCD and Special Use District, where a restaurant serving on-sale liquor (ABC Types 47, 41, etc.) is a conditional use requiring Planning Commission approval and a finding that it operates as a bona fide eating place (Planning Code §722 and §780.3(c)(2)(A)).
findings.verification_note: The records show restaurant_permission as 'unknown' and state the controls are in rule lines not shown; §780.3(c)(2)(A) does not appear in the cited records.

findings.text: Five Conditional Use Authorizations are on file at 401 Columbus Ave: 1988 (small restaurant), 1997 (full-service restaurant), 2004 (beer/wine to Type 47 upgrade), 2007 (expansion to 2,040 sq ft), and 2009 (specialty food self-service use), the most recent decided March 2010.

In May 2022 Planning approved an ABC referral for a Type 41 (beer/wine) license at this address for Cassava restaurant, stating per §780.3(c)(1)(B) that a restaurant may occupy a space last used as a restaurant, and noting that the prior occupant Trattoria Pinocchio was also a full-service restaurant.

At 414 Columbus Ave (43 m away), the Planning Commission in December 2022 approved a CUA to transfer a Type 47 license to Mona Lisa Mare e Monti restaurant, an existing restaurant upgrading from Type 41, taking 270 days from filing to approval.

basis.text: The licence looked up is ABC Type 47 (on-sale general, eating place), as stated in the description.
The licence is to be obtained by transfer from other premises (a premises-to-premises transfer), as the applicant states.

A Type 47 licence is an on-sale general licence. State law limits these to one for each 2,000 inhabitants of the county; in a county over that number ABC issues no additional one, so the licence comes by transfer of an existing licence unless state law allows otherwise.

North Beach Special Use District: A Restaurant may sell beer, wine or liquor for drinking on the premises (ABC licence Types 02, 23, 41, 47, 49, 59 or 75) only by Conditional Use on the First Story, with a Planning Commission finding that it is and will remain a Bona Fide Eating Place. Here: a conditional use (Planning Code § 780.3(c)(2)(A), in force since before 2022-01-01).

North Beach Special Use District: The 51% food-receipts test is gone; the Restaurant must give the Department records of its gross receipts or gross sales on request. This is a requirement, not a control (Planning Code § 780.3(c)(2)(A), in force from 2024-01-14 (Ord. 249-23, File No. 230701)).
Census tract 107.02: 22 active on-sale retail licences in ABC's licences as they stood on 10 December 2024, against 5 authorised in ABC's census tract authorisations of September 2026.

The tract is over its authorised number, and state law tests a transfer from other premises for undue concentration. The licence may still issue if public convenience or necessity would be served: public convenience or necessity finding likely required.

The liquor licence rule of the restricted district makes this licence a conditional use here, so it can be used only with a Conditional Use Authorization. ABC also investigates the application, and the applicant must post public notice: further review.
basis.code_section: Planning Code § 303; California Business and Professions Code §§ 23958 (investigation) and 23985 (public notice)

conditions: Signage: A sign permit and compliance with Article 6 of the Planning Code will be required. All exterior signage shall be designed to complement, not compete with, the existing architectural character and architectural features of the building. Monitoring - After Entitlement

Validity: The authorization and right vested by virtue of this action is valid for three (3) years from the effecti ve date of the Motion. The Department of Building Inspection shall have issued a Building Permit or Site Permit to construct the project and/or commence the approved use within this three-year period. (standard)

Expiration and Renewal: Should a Building or Site Permit be sought after the three (3) year period has lapsed, the project sponsor must seek a renewal of this Authorization by filing an application for an amendment to the original Authorization or a new application for Authorization. Should the project sponsor decline to so file, and decline to withdraw the permit application, the Commission shall conduct a public hearing in order to consider the revocation of the Authorization. (standard)

Diligent Pursuit: Once a site or Building Permit has been issued, construction must commence within the timeframe required by the Department of Building Inspection and be continued diligently to completion. Failure to do so shall be grounds for the Commission to consider revoking the approval if more than three (3) years have passed since this Authorization was approved. (standard)

Extension: All time limits in the preceding three paragraphs may be extended at the discretion of the Zoning Administrator where implementation of the project is delayed by a public agency, an appeal or a legal challenge and only by the length of time for which such public agency, appeal or challenge has caused delay . (standard)

Conformity with Current Law: No application for Building Permit, Site Permit, or other entitlement shall be approved unless it complies with all applicable provisions of City Codes in effect at the time of such approval. (standard)

Garbage, Composting and Recycling Storage: Space for the collection and storage of garbage, composting, and recycling shall be provided within enclosed areas on the property and clearly labeled and illustrated on the building permit plans. Space for the collection and storage of recyclable and compostable materials that meets the size, location, accessibility, and other standards specified by the San Francisco Recycling Program shall be provided at the ground level of the buildings. comparable_cases.why_comparable: 414 Columbus Ave (43 m away, same block) received CUA approval in December 2022 to transfer a Type 47 license to Mona Lisa Mare e Monti, an existing restaurant upgrading from Type 41. Nearly identical fact pattern: same North Beach NCD zoning, same corridor, Type 41→47 upgrade.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Use decision: Commission approved the Type 41→47 upgrade with standard conditions (signage, validity period, odor control, sidewalk maintenance, community liaison). Took 9 months from filing (March 2022) to decision (December 2022). Shows Commission does approve full-liquor upgrades on this corridor when restaurant operations are established.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 570 Green St (91 m away, North Beach NCD) received Planning approval for Type 47 in November 2024 as a continuation of existing restaurant use. Very recent (decided one month ago), same zoning district, same license type.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral: Planning approved Type 47 as 'continuation of existing use' in conjunction with an existing restaurant. This was an ABC referral not requiring CUA, likely because the restaurant already held Type 47 or the space had prior full-liquor authorization, distinguishing it from a new intensification.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 565 Green St (47 m away, North Beach NCD) approved Type 47 for Belle Cora restaurant in March 2023 as continuation of existing use. Same district, very close proximity, recent approval.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral: Planning approved Type 47 without CUA as a continuation of existing restaurant use. Pattern suggests that where a space has prior Type 47 history or where Planning deems it a true continuation (no change of business, no expansion), a referral suffices; new intensifications require CUA.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 1309 Grant Ave (90 m away, North Beach NCD) approved reinstatement of Type 47 in July 2023 for same owner/restaurant, noting no vacancy >18 months, no TI, no enlargement, and continued bona fide eating place operation.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral: Planning approved Type 47 without CUA when the restaurant had not been vacant >18 months, same owner, no TI or expansion. The decision text lists specific criteria that allow continuation without a new CUA; the subject concept meets some (no TI, existing restaurant space) but differs on intensification from lower alcohol to Type 47.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 674 Broadway (110 m away, Chinatown CCB district) approved Type 41 for a restaurant in March 2024. Different zoning but shows recent Planning approvals of alcohol licenses for restaurants in adjacent high-density entertainment areas.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral: Planning approved Type 41 as principally permitted for a restaurant.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 411 Columbus Ave (11 m away, adjacent parcel on same block) approved Type 41 for a restaurant in October 2021. Immediate neighbor, same NCD and SUD, continuation of existing use.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral: Planning approved Type 41 for continuation of restaurant use with no further expansion. The address is directly adjacent (11 m) to the subject property, confirming that alcohol service in restaurants is well-established and approved along this block face.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 658 Vallejo St (11 m away, North Beach NCD) approved Type 41 for a restaurant in October 2021, noting change of use to Restaurant approved 4/26/2021 per amendments to PC Sections 722 and 780.3 related to COVID Limited Restaurant conversions.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral: Planning approved a Limited Restaurant conversion to Restaurant with Type 41 under 2020 legislation that allowed conversions without CUA for established Bona Fide Eating Places. Shows Planning facilitated restaurant alcohol upgrades in North Beach during/after pandemic, though this was beer/wine not full liquor.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 414 Columbus Ave (43 m away, same address as the CUA comparable) approved a DPH Restaurant referral in April 2022, four months before the Type 47 CUA was filed. Shows the two-step process: health permit referral first, then CUA for alcohol intensification.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral: Planning approved continuation of existing Restaurant use for health permit purposes. This preceded the March 2022 filing of the Type 47 CUA (2022-002108CUA) at the same address, illustrating that operators at this address obtain health/DPH approval first, then file the CUA for alcohol upgrades.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 401 Columbus Ave (same address as subject property, 0 m) received CUA approval in May 1988 to establish a small self-service restaurant. This is the earliest recorded Planning approval at the subject address, establishing the restaurant use.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Use decision: Commission approved a restaurant at 401 Columbus in 1988. Combined with subsequent CUAs visible in the record summary (1997, 2004 Type 47 upgrade, 2007 expansion), the property has a 36-year continuous history of Commission-approved restaurant uses and intensifications, suggesting strong precedent for compatibility.

filing_playbook.action: Engage a California ABC license broker to identify, escrow and initiate transfer of an available Type 47 license to 401 Columbus Ave.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The broker handles the license purchase agreement, escrow, premises-to-premises transfer, posting at the premises. Budget $100k–$450k for the license purchase and 90–240 days total (catalog ca.abc_type_47).
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm in writing with SF Planning whether the restaurant concept is formula retail and obtain the five CUA motions on file at 401 Columbus Ave (Cases 1988.106C, 1997.365C, 2004.0925C, 2007.1256C, 2009.1079C) to review their conditions.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Email or visit SF Planning's public counter with the business name, ownership structure, and a statement of whether the restaurant shares its name, décor, menu, or standardized features with 11 or more other locations. Also request copies of the five CUA motions on file for 401 Columbus Ave to confirm which conditions remain in effect and whether any are proposed to be changed. Planning needs these answers to complete the CUA application, and formula retail is not permitted in the North Beach NCD so it must be ruled out before filing.

timeline_cost.notes: The timeline and cost are for the CUA, the Type 47 license transfer, and the health permit—the three approvals in the entitlement path—and assume they are granted. The CUA takes roughly 120–300 days from filing to Commission decision based on the December 2022 comparable at 414 Columbus Ave (270 days, app:datasf_planning:2022-002108CUA) and typical CUA timelines (catalog:sf.conditional_use_authorization equivalent). The Type 47 transfer takes 90–240 days including broker engagement, escrow, ABC posting, investigation, and license issuance (catalog:ca.abc_type_47), and costs $17,000–$450,000 for the license purchase on the open market plus ABC fees; the lower end assumes a distressed or rural-county license, the upper end reflects San Francisco market prices. The health permit takes 14–45 days after CUA approval (catalog:sf.health_permit, $470–$1,000). The CUA filing fee is approximately $3,100 (2026–27 estimate, scaled by construction cost; the concept states no tenant improvements so the base fee applies). Government fees total roughly $20,000–$24,000 (CUA + ABC transfer fee + health permit + business registration + entity formation + other state/local fees from the catalog); the wide cost range is driven entirely by the Type 47 license purchase price, which is a private-market transaction not a government fee. These figures do not include attorney, architect, or broker professional fees, which can add $15,000–$50,000 depending on complexity. The timeline assumes no appeals (a 30-day appeal period follows the CUA decision), no ABC hearing on the PCN issue (which would add 2–6 months), and no significant delays in neighborhood outreach or document preparation. If the formula retail question or the prior CUA condition-amendment question cannot be resolved, or if the Commission denies the CUA, the timeline and cost do not apply.

records_summary: 401 Columbus Ave sits in the North Beach NCD where a restaurant serving full liquor is a conditional use requiring Planning Commission approval (Planning Code §722 and §780.3). The space has a long history as a restaurant with multiple CUAs dating back to 1988, most recently approved for a Type 41 license in 2022 for Cassava restaurant. The block is extremely dense with 75 food/drink businesses within 500 ft, 46 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft, and 109 licenses within 1,000 ft—ABC's undue concentration flag is raised. The base rate shows only 6 dated use decisions within 1,000 ft over 5 years (1 approved, 4 approved with conditions, 1 withdrawn), too few to calculate an approval rate but suggesting conditional approvals are typical for alcohol intensifications here.
data_gaps: No ABC conditions are exposed for the active Type 47 licenses nearby, so cannot compare operating restrictions
